The strongest ground is that the promise was oral. Where a statute requires a signed writing to revive a time-barred debt, an oral promise to pay the $750 is unenforceable even though the debt was once owed. Lack of consideration is weaker, since Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 treats a promise to pay a barred debt as binding without new consideration, and the overheard "deadbeat" remark does not create duress or supply consideration.

CONFIDENCE: 70
